jobs.title: Director, Strategy and Operations
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 276793

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

The Role

This Director Level role is a strategic operational leader within the Enterprise Data and AI Platform organization, responsible for driving workforce optimization, engagement, communication, and innovation outcomes. This role enables the SVP & CIO’s strategic agenda by ensuring that human capital, vendor engagement, and organizational communications are optimized to deliver measurable value, efficiency, and cultural impact across a global technology function.  

The Director leads cross-functional initiatives spanning workforce strategy, contract and vendor optimization, communications and branding, and innovation and early talent development, ensuring alignment with Enterprise Data and AI Platform technology roadmap and operational priorities.

Is this role right for you? In this role you will:

Portfolio Strategy & Prioritization

Translate strategic priorities into an integrated portfolio roadmap, investment plan, and delivery priorities.
Maintain visibility of portfolio outcomes, milestones, investment decisions, and strategic trade-offs.
Support annual and multi-year planning processes, including roadmap and funding decisions.
Monitor delivery across initiatives, identifying cross-program dependencies, risks, constraints, and execution gaps.
Coordinate with program, product, engineering, architecture, risk, finance, and business teams to ensure portfolio alignment.
Drive disciplined management of scope, milestones, commitments, and portfolio-level outcomes.

Financial & Workforce Management

Manage portfolio budgets, forecasts, actuals, and financial performance.
Support business cases and investment decisions, including FTE, contractor, and vendor capacity requirements.
Track workforce demand and capacity against portfolio priorities.
Identify opportunities to optimize spend, reduce duplication, and improve return on investment.

Executive Reporting & Insights

Develop concise executive and SteerCo reporting on portfolio health, delivery progress, investments, risks, and decisions required.
Provide data-driven insights and recommendations to senior leadership.
Establish portfolio KPIs and reporting that connect delivery progress with measurable business outcomes.
Ensure risks and emerging issues are surfaced early with clear mitigation and decision paths

Metrics, Dashboards, And Reporting

Own design and governance for Enterprise Data and AI Platform’s dashboarding framework, ensuring timely, accurate, and insightful reporting for executives.  
Track and communicate key performance indicators (KPIs) and key risk indicators (KRIs) across workforce capacity, engagement, financial optimization, and innovation delivery.  
Partner with data and analytics teams to enhance automation, transparency, and decision support for CIO and leadership forums.  

Strategic & Operational Leadership

Contribute to strategic planning cycles, leadership offsites, and transformation programs.  
Represent the Enterprise Data and AI Platform strategy and operations function across enterprise technology leadership forums.  

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We'd love to work with you if you have:

Bachelor’s degree in business, Human Resources, Communications, or a related field; MBA preferred.  
10+ years of experience in workforce management, operations, or strategic communications ideally within technology, financial services, or a professional services environment.  
Proven ability to lead cross-functional programs with measurable business impact and stakeholder alignment.  
Strong financial and contractual acumen with demonstrated experience optimizing vendor and resource portfolios.  
Superior storytelling, communication, and presentation skills with experience representing senior technology leaders.  
Familiarity using analytics and visualization tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau) to drive workforce and performance insights.  
Strategic thinker with a collaborative and execution-oriented leadership style.

What's in it for you?

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion & Allyship - We strive to create an inclusive culture where every employee is empowered to reach their fullest potential, respected for who they are, and are embraced through bias-free practices and inclusive values across Scotiabank. We embrace diversity and provide opportunities for all employee to learn, grow & participate through our various Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that span across diverse gender identities, ethnicity, race, age, ability & veterans.
Accessibility and Workplace Accommodations - We value the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the Bank, and are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Scotiabank continues to locate, remove and prevent barriers so that we can build a diverse and inclusive environment while meeting accessibility requirements.
Upskilling through online courses, cross-functional development opportunities, and tuition assistance.
Competitive Rewards program including bonus, flexible vacation, personal, sick days and benefits will start on day one.
Dynamic Ecosystem - Free tea & coffee, universal washrooms, and lots of space for team collaboration.
Community Engagement - No matter where you choose to work from; we offer opportunities for community engagement & belonging with our various programs.

Location(s): Canada : Ontario : Toronto

Scotiabank is a leading bank in the Americas. Guided by our purpose: "for every future", we help our customers, their families and their communities achieve success through a broad range of advice, products and services, including personal and commercial banking, wealth management and private banking, corporate and investment banking, and capital markets.

At Scotiabank, we value the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the Bank, and are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. If you require accommodation (including, but not limited to, an accessible interview site, alternate format documents, ASL Interpreter, or Assistive Technology) during the recruitment and selection process, please let our Recruitment team know. If you require technical assistance, please click here. Candidates must apply directly online to be considered for this role. We thank all applicants for their interest in a career at Scotiabank; however, only those candidates who are selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Chief Information Officer (CIO)
jobs.description:
Buckland is looking for a Chief Information Officer (CIO)

What You’ll Be Doing

This position is responsible for delivering best-in-class, customer-focused technology, and security leading the development, technology, and cybersecurity teams. This role will be accountable for providing the vision, oversight, and execution of the organization's technology and cyber security strategy to align with strategic organizational goals and modernization objectives.

What We Can Offer You

Competitive, salary, benefits package, and matching retirement savings plan.
A friendly, collaborative work environment.
Opportunities for professional development & ongoing learning.
A chance to be part of a growing organization.
Remote work arrangement available for applicants who are not local to a Buckland office.

You will be responsible for

Collaborate with the senior leadership team to determine, prioritize, and execute the overall business strategy
Develop, implement, review, and monitor departmental and project KPI’s to budget.
Lead software and product development while adopting methodologies such as Agile to deliver high-performing, scalable solutions on time and within budget.
Plan/implement evaluation process for technical architecture and system management
Develop and implements the overall technology strategy for the organization, including 1-year, 3-year, and 5-year roadmaps
Lead the transformation of how information is distributed/communicated internally
Establish strong relationships with IT providers and external vendors to improve the company’s information technology systems
Ensure projects are staffed, budgeted, and delivered on target using internal and external resources
Responsible for data security, management, and governance ensuring business continuity in a 24/7 environment.
Build out a multi-year Cyber Security roadmap
Develop, implement, and test disaster recovery and IT security failure procedures
Oversee and enhance systems analysis, programming, and project management across ERP, core, database, and departmental applications

Leadership Responsibilities

Clear, concise and transparent communication keeping all parties informed about developments, ensuring alignment with organizational goals
Leverages technological innovations to streamline lines of businesses, enhance internal/external customer experiences and drives efficiencies
Fosters collaboration, continuous improvement and innovation creating of employee satisfaction
Assess risks and benefits and implements comprehensive risk management strategies, safeguarding the organization regardless of challenges
Strong literacy and analytical skills understanding financial statements and utilizing financial data to drive decisions for best results

What We Need From You

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology/Computer Science or a related field.
Master’s degree in Science, Information Technology or related field
Minimum 15 years of experience, including 5+ years of experience in providing strategic and inclusive leadership
Experience in scaling technology teams managing multiple products across multiple lines of business
Experience with Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL-4) framework
Experience deploying architecture and systems with requiring high availability and cost efficiency
Skilled in entrepreneurship, strategy development, complex project management, and identifying and executing solutions
Strong knowledge with Microsoft technology stack and data analytics platforms such as Power BI
Must be legally eligible to work for the Company at all times.
Valid Passport and ability to travel if required to other offices locations in CAD/USA/MEX.

jobs.title: Director, Revenue Operations, Enterprise
jobs.description:
Clio is the global leader in legal AI technology, empowering legal professionals and law firms of every size to work smarter, faster, and more securely.

We are transforming the legal experience for all by bettering the lives of legal professionals while increasing access to justice.

Summary:

We are currently seeking a Director of Revenue Operations, Enterprise
to join our Revenue Operations
team preferably in Toronto, Calgary, Vancouver, or remotely across the U.S. or Canada (excluding Québec).

What your team does:

Revenue Operations has one job—to drive growth by accelerating our revenue-generating teams. We directly support Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success by providing insights, reducing friction, and enabling teams to be innovative and self-sufficient.

About The Role

Clio is at an inflection point. With the strategic acquisitions of ShareDo and vLex, we are significantly expanding our enterprise footprint and investing in the dedicated operational leadership to match that ambition. The Director of Enterprise Revenue Operations will be the single operational owner responsible for scaling and maturing our Enterprise GTM motion end-to-end — from Sales Operations through to Customer Success operations — ensuring our Enterprise business runs with the speed, precision, and sophistication that our customers and growth targets demand.

This is a builder role. You will stand up the operational infrastructure, processes, and team that power Clio's enterprise segment. Reporting to the VP, Revenue Operations and partnering directly with the SVP of Enterprise, you will work in close collaboration with Clio's RevOps functional leaders to ensure enterprise execution is tightly integrated with the broader GTM engine.

What you'll work on:

Enterprise GTM Operations

Build and lead the Enterprise Revenue Operations team, covering Sales, CS Operations and Analytics.
Partner with the SVP of Enterprise to design and execute GTM strategies that enable the enterprise segment to scale
Establish enterprise sales processes, operating cadences, and Rules of Engagement, and work with enablement to operationalize programs that equip GTM teams to execute across the full customer lifecycle
Own enterprise post-sales operations, ensuring onboarding, adoption, renewal, expansion and professional services processes are built for enterprise complexity and scale
Ensure enterprise tooling integrates into Clio's core tech stack, partnering with the Director of GTM Applications and SMB Revenue Operations leadership team

Enterprise Product and GTM Alignment

Partner with Product, Product Marketing and Enterprise leadership to operationalize GTM strategies across Clio’s suite including Vincent and Clio Operate
Ensure pricing, packaging and sales motions support enterprise buyers adopting multiple products across the customer lifecycle
Develop operational frameworks that support cross-sell and expansion within complex enterprise environments

Forecasting, Planning & Performance

Own pipeline and ARR forecasting across the enterprise segment, establishing the methodology and cadences that give leadership visibility into risk and upside
Lead territory design, segmentation, quota allocation, and capacity planning, translating growth targets into actionable coverage models
Own incentive compensation design in partnership with the Director of Compensation for the enterprise GTM organization, partnering with Finance and HR to ensure plans drive the right behaviors
Lead QBRs, MBRs and executive reporting, translating performance data into clear insights and recommendations for senior leadership

GTM Data & Insights

Define how GTM metrics are measured, distributed, and actioned across the enterprise segment; covering pipeline health, conversion, retention, expansion, and efficiency
Partner with Data & Finance to maintain clean, consistent GTM data infrastructure and support board-level reporting
Own analytics and build the analytics muscle for Enterprise

What you bring:

Bachelor's degree; MBA preferred
7+ years as a Senior Manager of RevOps or 3+ years as a Director of RevOps in a B2B SaaS environment
Experience building or scaling Enterprise GTM operations, ideally in a company moving upmarket
Management experience required — 3+ direct reports
Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate complex data into clear recommendations for senior leadership
Comfortable in a matrix environment — influencing without direct authority across multiple functional teams
Roll-up-your-sleeves mentality — this is a builder role, not a manager-only role
Proficiency with core GTM tools including Salesforce, SalesLoft, Gong, CPQ platforms, and familiarity with Professional Services Automation (PSA) and Customer Success platforms
Ability to travel to or within Canada one week per quarter

This role is a backfill for an existing position.

What you will find here:

Compensation is one of the main components of Clio’s Total Rewards Program. We have developed a series of programs and processes to ensure we are creating fair and competitive pay practices that form the foundation of our human and high-performing culture.

Some highlights of our Total Rewards program include:

Competitive, equitable salary with top-tier health benefits, dental, and vision insurance
Hybrid work environment, with expectation for local Clions (Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Dublin, London, New York City and Sydney) to be in office min. twice per week.
Flexible time off policy, with an encouraged 20 days off per year.
$2000 annual counseling benefit
RRSP matching and RESP contribution
Clioversary recognition program with special acknowledgement at 3, 5, 7, and 10 years

The on-target earnings (OTE) salary range for this role is $220,400 to $330,600 reflecting base salary plus variable compensation at 100% attainment. Variable compensation is not guaranteed and will depend on individual, team, or company performance. Initial placement within the range is informed by geographic region, experience, and skillset, with room to progress as impact and tenure grow. Final offer amounts will vary based on candidate profile.

Diversity, Inclusion, Belonging and Equity (DIBE) & Accessibility

Our team shows up as their authentic selves, and are united by our mission. We are dedicated to diversity, equity and inclusion. We pride ourselves in building and fostering an environment where our teams feel included, valued, and enabled to do the best work of their careers, wherever they choose to log in from. We believe that different perspectives, skills, backgrounds, and experiences result in higher-performing teams and better innovation. We are committed to equal employment and we encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

Clio provides accessibility accommodations during the recruitment process. Should you require any accommodation, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

Learn more about our culture at clio.com/careers

However, we've built our systems to ensure that a human always reviews AI-generated output, and we never make automated hiring decisions.

jobs.title: Vice President of Finance And Operations
jobs.description:
BoomerangFX

Location:
Mississauga, Ontario — on-site, five days per week
Reports to:
Chief Executive Officer

Mandatory Experience

A Canadian CPA designation and hands-on experience leading finance and operations for a PE-backed SaaS company scaling ARR from $10 million to $50 million are mandatory. Only applicants meeting these requirements will be considered for the role.

Why Join BoomerangFX?

BoomerangFX is a global healthcare technology company bringing SaaS, artificial intelligence and digital marketing together to help private-pay healthcare practices operate and grow. Recognized through Deloitte’s Technology Fast 500 program, we are building technology that simplifies practice management, strengthens patient engagement and helps healthcare businesses reach more people.
With operations in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia and India
, we are scaling internationally and working at the forefront of AI in healthcare. Our teams collaborate across countries and disciplines to turn new ideas into products and services that make a practical difference for customers.

Joining BoomerangFX is an opportunity to build your career alongside a growing global business. You will have meaningful responsibility, exposure to international markets and the opportunity to contribute ideas, develop your skills and see the impact of your work. We welcome people who take ownership, move quickly and want to help build what comes next.

The Role

Reporting to the CEO, you will lead financial management and general operations with strong financial acumen, commercial judgment and a practical approach to execution
.

You will directly oversee the Controller and Accountant
and take responsibility for talent acquisition, human resources, vendor negotiations and corporate infrastructure
.

You will also attend and present at board meetings and lead strategic planning with the CEO
, connecting growth priorities with disciplined financial and operational execution.

Financial Leadership and Accounting Oversight

Directly oversee the Controller and Accountant, setting clear expectations for accuracy, reporting deadlines, financial controls and accountability. Review their work and provide hands-on guidance on complex issues.
Own the quality and timeliness of monthly, quarterly and annual financial reporting. Review financial statements, balance-sheet reconciliations, management reports and material accounting judgments.
Oversee billing, subscription revenue recognition, deferred revenue, collections, accounts payable, payroll and intercompany reporting. Maintain clear controls over approvals, payments and financial records.
Coordinate external accountants, auditors and tax advisers, and strengthen accounting policies and controls as the company scales.

Financial Performance and Cash Management

Lead annual budgeting, rolling forecasts, financial modelling and variance analysis. Challenge assumptions and translate financial results into clear recommendations for the CEO and department leaders.
Own a rolling 13-week cash-flow forecast and longer-term liquidity projections. Improve collections, working capital, spending discipline and visibility into financial commitments.
Analyze profitability by product, service and market. Use SaaS metrics, including ARR, retention, churn, gross margin, customer acquisition cost and payback, to evaluate performance and investment decisions.
Assess hiring plans, pricing, operating costs and major expenditures against expected returns. Drive measurable improvements in margins, productivity and progress toward sustainable profitability.

Talent Acquisition and Human Resources

Oversee talent acquisition and human resources, including internal staff and external providers. Align recruitment priorities and headcount plans with approved budgets and business needs.
Oversee recruitment execution, agency relationships, hiring timelines, onboarding and workforce planning. Hold hiring managers accountable for clear requirements, timely decisions and hiring outcomes.
Oversee HR administration, employee records, compensation and benefits coordination, performance-review processes, employee relations and offboarding, working with qualified advisers where required.

Vendor Negotiations and Corporate Infrastructure

Lead vendor negotiations and oversee procurement, contracts and renewals. Secure commercially sound pricing, payment terms and service commitments, and hold providers accountable for delivery.
Oversee corporate infrastructure, including offices, facilities, equipment, business systems and outsourced services. Ensure these resources support reliable daily operations and future growth.
Work with technology leaders on corporate IT providers, software licenses, infrastructure spending and business continuity arrangements. Improve utilization and eliminate unnecessary or duplicate costs.

Operating Performance and Team Leadership

Establish operating KPIs, management dashboards and regular performance reviews across finance and the functions under your oversight.
Improve workflows, approval processes and reporting through practical automation and stronger data quality. Ensure corrective actions have accountable owners and deadlines.
Lead and develop the finance team and collaborate with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Product and Technology leaders to improve execution and resource allocation.

Board Participation and Reporting

Attend board meetings and present financial and operational results, forecasts, liquidity, material risks and recommended actions.

Own the preparation and quality of board financial packages and performance presentations. Explain the drivers of results and material variances against plan.
Support the CEO in discussions with directors and investors, respond to questions with clear analysis, and ensure actions within your remit are followed through.

Strategic Planning

Lead annual and multiyear strategic planning with the CEO
, translating business priorities into financial targets, operating plans, investment decisions and measurable milestones.
Develop scenario models and recommendations on growth, profitability, capital allocation, organizational capacity and international expansion.
Evaluate financing, partnerships, acquisitions and other strategic opportunities with the CEO. Ensure approved initiatives are financially sound and supported by execution plans.

Mandatory Qualifications

CPA designation in good standing in Canada.

At least 10 years of progressive finance experience, including hands-on leadership across financial reporting, controllership, budgeting, forecasting, cash management and operating performance.

BoomerangFX

Mississauga, Ontario — on-site, five days per week
Reports to:
Chief Executive Officer

Mandatory Experience

A Canadian CPA designation and hands-on experience leading finance and operations for a PE-backed SaaS company scaling ARR from $5 million to $50 million are mandatory. Only applicants meeting these requirements will be considered for the role.

Why Join BoomerangFX?

BoomerangFX is a global healthcare technology company bringing SaaS, artificial intelligence and digital marketing together to help private-pay healthcare practices operate and grow. Recognized through Deloitte’s Technology Fast 500 program, we are building technology that simplifies practice management, strengthens patient engagement and helps healthcare businesses reach more people.
With operations in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia and India
, we are scaling internationally and working at the forefront of AI in healthcare. Our teams collaborate across countries and disciplines to turn new ideas into products and services that make a practical difference for customers.

Joining BoomerangFX is an opportunity to build your career alongside a growing global business. You will have meaningful responsibility, exposure to international markets and the opportunity to contribute ideas, develop your skills and see the impact of your work. We welcome people who take ownership, move quickly and want to help build what comes next.

The Role

Reporting to the CEO, you will lead financial management and general operations with strong financial acumen, commercial judgment and a practical approach to execution
.

You will oversee the Controller and Accountant
while taking responsibility for talent acquisition, human resources, vendor negotiations and corporate infrastructure
. You must be comfortable reviewing the detail, challenging assumptions and resolving issues personally while building an accountable team.

Financial Leadership and Accounting Oversight

Directly oversee the Controller and Accountant, setting clear expectations for accuracy, reporting deadlines, financial controls and accountability. Review their work and provide hands-on guidance on complex issues.
Own the quality and timeliness of monthly, quarterly and annual financial reporting. Review financial statements, balance-sheet reconciliations, management reports and material accounting judgments.
Oversee billing, subscription revenue recognition, deferred revenue, collections, accounts payable, payroll and intercompany reporting. Maintain clear controls over approvals, payments and financial records.
Coordinate external accountants, auditors and tax advisers, and strengthen accounting policies and controls as the company scales.

Financial Performance and Cash Management

Lead annual budgeting, rolling forecasts, financial modelling and variance analysis. Challenge assumptions and translate financial results into clear recommendations for the CEO and department leaders.
Own a rolling 13-week cash-flow forecast and longer-term liquidity projections. Improve collections, working capital, spending discipline and visibility into financial commitments.
Analyze profitability by product, service and market. Use SaaS metrics, including ARR, retention, churn, gross margin, customer acquisition cost and payback, to evaluate performance and investment decisions.
Assess hiring plans, pricing, operating costs and major expenditures against expected returns. Drive measurable improvements in margins, productivity and progress toward sustainable profitability.

Oversee recruitment execution, agency relationships, hiring timelines, onboarding and workforce planning. Hold hiring managers accountable for clear requirements, timely decisions and hiring outcomes.
Oversee HR administration, employee records, compensation and benefits coordination, performance-review processes, employee relations and offboarding, working with qualified advisers where required.

Lead vendor negotiations and oversee procurement, contracts and renewals. Secure commercially sound pricing, payment terms and service commitments, and hold providers accountable for delivery.
Oversee corporate infrastructure, including offices, facilities, equipment, business systems and outsourced services. Ensure these resources support reliable daily operations and future growth.
Work with technology leaders on corporate IT providers, software licences, infrastructure spending and business continuity arrangements. Improve utilization and eliminate unnecessary or duplicate costs.

Establish operating KPIs, management dashboards and regular performance reviews across finance and the functions under your oversight.
Improve workflows, approval processes and reporting through practical automation and stronger data quality. Ensure corrective actions have accountable owners and deadlines.
Lead and develop the finance team and collaborate with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Product and Technology leaders to improve execution and resource allocation.

CPA designation in good standing in Canada.

jobs.description:
Job Description

The Senior Director, Community Information Security Governance (the “Sr Director”) is a vital leadership role, hired by and receiving full benefits through the Jewish Federation of British Columbia (JFBC), in order to lead JFBC’s Community Cybersecurity Program (the “Program”), a community-wide initiative supporting the cybersecurity resilience of Jewish community organizations in British Columbia.

The Sr Director is responsible for developing, implementing, and managing a comprehensive cybersecurity program to safeguard the critical information assets of JFBC and of community organizations participating in the Program. This key role will oversee all aspects of information security, ensuring the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data across the Program and its participating organizations.

Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To

Develop, implement, and maintain a strategic information security program aligned with industry best practices and regulatory frameworks.
Oversee and/or conduct security risk assessments and implement controls to mitigate identified vulnerabilities.
Guide participating community organizations with their cybersecurity requirements.
Oversee the development and enforcement of security policies, procedures, and standards.
Manage security awareness and training programs for staff across JFBC and organizations participating in the Program.
Assist in assembling an incident response team and provide consultative guidance during the incident response process in the event of a security breach.
Oversee the design and implementation of services designed to reduce cybersecurity risks across JFBC and participating community organizations using best practices in project management.
Collaborate with IT teams to ensure the secure design and implementation of technology systems.
Stay abreast of evolving cybersecurity threats and trends and implement appropriate safeguards.
Coordinates and manages relationships with organizations participating or prospectively participating in the Program.
Communicate effectively with senior management and participating organizations on security risks and mitigation strategies.
Develop, present and oversee the financial budget for all expenditures and advocate for necessary resources, ensuring alignment with Program goals and objectives.

Qualifications

Minimum 7-10 years of experience in information security, with a proven track record of success in leading and managing security programs
Experience in business development and communications
Demonstrated leadership and organizational skills
Strong project management skills, including experience planning, launching, and tracking multi-organization initiatives
Professional certifications in cybersecurity (e.g., ISC2 CISSP, ISACA CISM, or EC Council CCISO), PMP (or equivalent)
In-depth knowledge of cybersecurity best practices and globally adopted frameworks (e.g., NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ISO 27001), and Canadian Centre for Cyber Security Baseline Controls
Experience in conducting security risk assessments and implementing security controls
Excellent communication, collaboration, and interpersonal skills
Strong understanding of the Jewish Community, non-profit sector, and their unique security challenges is an asset

About Us

Jewish Federation of British Columbia is the central planning, convening, facilitating, and fundraising organization for the local Jewish community and works collaboratively with more than three dozen partner organizations, unifying their work.

Together, we touch the lives of thousands of community members—Jewish and non-Jewish—locally, in Israel, and around the world.

Our Work Is Inspired By The Following Core Values

Chesed – loving kindness
Tzedakah – justice, charity
Klal Israel – unity of the Jewish people
Tikkun Olam – repairing the world

Why Work For Jewish Federation

Meaningful work that strengthens and protects the Jewish community, locally, throughout BC and in Israel
A sincere and supportive workplace culture grounded in collaboration, excellence, and care
Investment in employee growth through training and professional development

Benefits

Extended Healthcare, including Vision & Dental
Life & Travel Insurance
RRSP Match
4 Weeks Paid Vacation in addition to Jewish Holiday, and Statutory Holiday Closures
Early Office Closures at 3 PM on Fridays
Competitive Maternity/Paternal Leave Bridging & Top-Up after 2 years of service
Free Staff Parking
Membership Discount to the Jewish Community Centre of Vancouver

Details And How To Apply

Annual salary: $140,000
Schedule: Full-time, Permanent - based on a 35-hour work week
Work location: In-person, Vancouver

If you are interested in this opportunity, please email your resume and cover letter (quoting “Senior Director, Community Information Security Governance” in the subject line) to hr@jewishbc.ca. Tell us how you can use your skills to benefit our team and our community!

Resumes that do not include a cover letter will not be considered. We thank all applicants; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

Jewish Federation is committed to equal opportunity and equal treatment for every prospective and current employee. We value diversity in the workplace and believe our work is stronger when it benefits from the experience and knowledge of a diverse team.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
Most finance leaders can tell you what happened. We need someone who can help determine what happens next.

Are You Ready to Build a Platform Company?

EDL Building Solutions is a strong, growing building services company today. Over the next five to seven years, we intend to become a platform company through acquisition, disciplined integration, and organic growth. This is a ground floor seat in building it. You will join the senior leadership team at the point where the decisions you make shape what EDL becomes, not just how it reports.

We are looking for a Director of Finance who is equally comfortable setting long term financial strategy, evaluating an acquisition, and rolling up their sleeves to fix an immediate problem. Reporting to the Vice President and partnering with the President, you will lead Finance, Human Resources, and Information Technology, three functions that must work together to make growth repeatable.

Who We Are

EDL Building Solutions is Alberta's trusted multi trade partner, providing HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and building automation solutions for commercial and industrial facilities. We give our clients peace of mind through reliability, comfort, and efficiency.

The Person We're Looking For

A Fixer.
You do not accept broken processes, recurring inefficiencies, or unexplained results as part of doing business. You find root causes, challenge existing practices, and own the improvement.

A Thinker.
You are analytical, commercially minded, and naturally curious. You look past the financial statements to understand what is really happening in the business, and you turn that understanding into practical recommendations.

A Doer.
You move between strategy and execution without losing either. You can lead a financial strategy discussion in the morning and work directly with your team to solve an operational issue in the afternoon.

What You'll Do

Partner with the Vice President and President on strategy, governance, and the decisions that shape EDL's future.
Lead Finance, HR, and IT, building the systems, structure, and capability to support growth.
Own financial reporting, budgeting, and rolling forecasts that look forward, not just backward.
Drive enterprise value through sustainable earnings, recurring revenue, cash generation, and return on invested capital.
Lead the financial side of acquisitions, including valuation, due diligence, financing, and post acquisition integration.
Manage inter-company transactions across operating entities and holding companies, including allocations, eliminations, and consolidated reporting.
Support the design and administration of the company wide short term incentive and bonus plan, including calculation and payout.
Manage cash flow, working capital, and treasury, including banking and lender relationships.
Partner with operational leaders on margins, labour utilization, job costing, pricing, and overhead, and challenge the numbers when they do not add up.
Lead, coach, and develop the Finance, HR, and IT teams, and hold them to clear standards of accountability.

What You Bring

A professional accounting designation (CPA or equivalent).
Progressive finance leadership experience, including several years leading a finance function at a senior level.
Multi entity and inter-company accounting experience, including holding company structures and consolidation.
Hands on mergers and acquisitions experience: valuation, due diligence, financing, and integration.
Experience leading or overseeing functions beyond finance, ideally HR and IT.
Strong commercial judgement and the confidence to challenge senior leaders constructively.
Experience with Jonas ERP software, particularly job costing, service management, project accounting, and financial reporting, is considered a strong asset.
Experience across construction, service, or a comparable multi trade environment will set you apart.

What You'll Get

Annual base salary: $130,000 - $180,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications.
Target short term incentive (STIP): 20% of annual base salary, subject to plan terms and performance.
Company paid benefits package and life insurance.
Paid vacation and paid personal time off.
RRSP matching.
The opportunity to build enterprise value, and share in the result.

Other Requirements

Valid driver's licence and a clean criminal record.
Based primarily out of EDL's Edmonton office.

Ready to Build Something Great?

If you are ready to help take EDL from a strong building services company to a platform company, we would like to hear from you.

Apply today. Our HR team reviews applications daily and will connect with qualified candidates to discuss next steps.

EDL Building Solutions | Reliability. Passion. One Team. Results.

Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders and executive leadership.
Demonstrated ability to build collaborative relationships, influence decision-making, and foster cross-functional alignment across academic, administrative, and internal IT teams.

Commitment to continuous improvement, innovation, and leading transformational initiatives that enhance technology service delivery, efficiency, and institutional success.

new_jobs.title: Director of Finance
new_jobs.description:
Most finance leaders can tell you what happened. We need someone who can help determine what happens next.

Are You Ready to Build a Platform Company?

EDL Building Solutions is a strong, growing building services company today. Over the next five to seven years, we intend to become a platform company through acquisition, disciplined integration, and organic growth. This is a ground floor seat in building it. You will join the senior leadership team at the point where the decisions you make shape what EDL becomes, not just how it reports.

We are looking for a Director of Finance who is equally comfortable setting long term financial strategy, evaluating an acquisition, and rolling up their sleeves to fix an immediate problem. Reporting to the Vice President and partnering with the President, you will lead Finance, Human Resources, and Information Technology, three functions that must work together to make growth repeatable.

Who We Are

EDL Building Solutions is Alberta's trusted multi trade partner, providing HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and building automation solutions for commercial and industrial facilities. We give our clients peace of mind through reliability, comfort, and efficiency.

The Person We're Looking For

A Fixer.
You do not accept broken processes, recurring inefficiencies, or unexplained results as part of doing business. You find root causes, challenge existing practices, and own the improvement.

A Thinker.
You are analytical, commercially minded, and naturally curious. You look past the financial statements to understand what is really happening in the business, and you turn that understanding into practical recommendations.

A Doer.
You move between strategy and execution without losing either. You can lead a financial strategy discussion in the morning and work directly with your team to solve an operational issue in the afternoon.

What You'll Do

Partner with the Vice President and President on strategy, governance, and the decisions that shape EDL's future.
Lead Finance, HR, and IT, building the systems, structure, and capability to support growth.
Own financial reporting, budgeting, and rolling forecasts that look forward, not just backward.
Drive enterprise value through sustainable earnings, recurring revenue, cash generation, and return on invested capital.
Lead the financial side of acquisitions, including valuation, due diligence, financing, and post acquisition integration.
Manage inter-company transactions across operating entities and holding companies, including allocations, eliminations, and consolidated reporting.
Support the design and administration of the company wide short term incentive and bonus plan, including calculation and payout.
Manage cash flow, working capital, and treasury, including banking and lender relationships.
Partner with operational leaders on margins, labour utilization, job costing, pricing, and overhead, and challenge the numbers when they do not add up.
Lead, coach, and develop the Finance, HR, and IT teams, and hold them to clear standards of accountability.

What You Bring

A professional accounting designation (CPA or equivalent).
Progressive finance leadership experience, including several years leading a finance function at a senior level.
Multi entity and inter-company accounting experience, including holding company structures and consolidation.
Hands on mergers and acquisitions experience: valuation, due diligence, financing, and integration.
Experience leading or overseeing functions beyond finance, ideally HR and IT.
Strong commercial judgement and the confidence to challenge senior leaders constructively.
Experience with Jonas ERP software, particularly job costing, service management, project accounting, and financial reporting, is considered a strong asset.
Experience across construction, service, or a comparable multi trade environment will set you apart.

What You'll Get

Annual base salary: $130,000 - $180,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications.
Target short term incentive (STIP): 20% of annual base salary, subject to plan terms and performance.
Company paid benefits package and life insurance.
Paid vacation and paid personal time off.
RRSP matching.
The opportunity to build enterprise value, and share in the result.

Other Requirements

Valid driver's licence and a clean criminal record.
Based primarily out of EDL's Edmonton office.

Ready to Build Something Great?

If you are ready to help take EDL from a strong building services company to a platform company, we would like to hear from you.

Apply today. Our HR team reviews applications daily and will connect with qualified candidates to discuss next steps.

EDL Building Solutions | Reliability. Passion. One Team. Results.

Job Overview

Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, the Director provides strategic and operational leadership across a broad portfolio of enterprise technology services, including network infrastructure, cloud platforms, data centres, enterprise computing, audiovisual technologies, and end-user support. Leading a team of managers and technical professionals, the Director fosters a collaborative, high-performing environment focused on continuous improvement, operational efficiency, and exceptional service delivery.

As a key member of KPU's IT leadership team, the Director plays an integral role in shaping and executing long-term technology strategies, advancing infrastructure modernization, and identifying opportunities to enhance the reliability, security, and effectiveness of university-wide systems. Working closely with academic and administrative leaders, the Director translates institutional priorities into innovative, sustainable technology solutions while overseeing strategic planning, disaster recovery, resource management, and operational and capital budgets.

This role offers the opportunity to shape KPU’s technology landscape, strengthen operational excellence, and drive strategic initiatives that support the university’s long-term goals.

At KPU, you'll be part of a purpose-driven environment that values innovation, continuous learning, work-life balance, and employee well-being. If you're a forward-thinking technology leader who thrives on building high-performing teams, driving meaningful change, and making a lasting impact, we'd love to hear from you!

Education And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in computer science or information technology;
A minimum of 12 years of progressive IT experience, with at least 7 years in a senior technology leadership capacity;
Minimum 2-years’ experience leading a service desk team.
Experience working within a post-secondary or public sector environment is preferred.
Experience managing enterprise desktop computing environments including laptops, desktops, and Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI);
Strong experience in developing, executing, and maintaining multi-year technology roadmaps aligned to institutional strategic plans;
Practical experience in datacenter, systems, and enterprise network architecture, operations, and lifecycle management, leveraging best practices and tools, including major cloud providers (e.g., AWS, Azure, or equivalent);
Information Technology Infrastructure Library certification is an asset;
Or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Demonstrated experience leading enterprise infrastructure modernization initiatives, including cloud adoption, cybersecurity best practices, and operational transformation.
Proven success deploying, managing, and evolving enterprise infrastructure technologies, including networks, data centers, storage, servers, and audiovisual systems.
Knowledge and experience in managing telecommunications technologies in an enterprise environment.
Familiarity with Audio-Visual technologies within enterprise environments.
Strategic and forward-looking thinker with a demonstrated ability to develop and implement innovative technology solutions that align with long-term institutional objectives.
Strong leadership and team-building capabilities, with proven success leading, motivating, and mentoring high-performing teams within unionized or public sector environments.
Expertise in high availability system design and operations, ensuring the continuity and resilience of mission-critical services and systems.
Skilled in complex contract negotiation, vendor management, performance monitoring, and overseeing service agreements.
Expertise in developing business cases, forecasting financials, and budget management.
Exceptional organizational and project oversight skills, including resource allocation, and timeline control across large, multi-stakeholder initiatives.
Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders and executive leadership.
Demonstrated ability to build collaborative relationships, influence decision-making, and foster cross-functional alignment across academic, administrative, and internal IT teams.
Ability to manage multiple competing priorities effectively.
Commitment to continuous improvement, innovation, and leading transformational initiatives that enhance technology service delivery, efficiency, and institutional success.
Ability to travel between campuses is required.

Competencies

Leadership: KPU employees inspire, coach, mentor, and support students, employees and KPU as a whole in achieving objectives.
Accountability: KPU employees demonstrate fiscal accountability and take ownership for their actions, decisions and results.
Continuous Improvement: KPU employees take a creative approach to opportunities, exploring unique ways to create optimal value for the KPU community.
Collaboration: KPU employees work in functional and cross-functional teams, coming together to solve complex issues and accomplish objectives that will benefit the KPU community.
